title: Glass transition temperature from the chemical structure of conjugated polymers
abstract: A single effective-mobility parameter relates Tg to molecular structure across 32 semiflexible conjugated polymers differing in aromatic backbone and alkyl side-chain chemistry; rigid conjugated backbones raise Tg while flexible alkyl side chains lower it (RMSE 13 C).

title: Machine learning discovery of high-temperature polymers
abstract: A deep neural network trained on ~6,900 experimental Tg values using Morgan fingerprints screened ~1M hypothetical polymers and identified >65,000 candidates with Tg > 200 C; rigid aromatic backbones dominate high-Tg designs.

title: Designing Polyimides with Desired Glass-Transition Temperature
abstract: From 878 polyimides with measured Tg, SMILES-derived descriptors and a neural network (RMSE ~11 K) show backbone rigidity and steric hindrance raise Tg; chain flexibility lowers it. Designed high-Tg polyimides verified experimentally.

title: Interpreting Molecular Descriptors for Glass Transition Temperature of Polyimides
abstract: A QSPR model unifies Tg descriptors under free-volume theory: molecular branching increases free volume and lowers Tg, while rigid, strongly interacting backbones give high Tg. Rotatable bonds correlate with processable low-Tg polymers.

title: Prediction and Interpretability of Polyimide Glass Transition Temperature (Tg-QSPR)
abstract: On 1257 polyimides with DSC Tg, RDKit descriptors and CatBoost (R2 0.82, MAE 20 C) identify NumRotatableBonds as highly influential and negatively correlated with Tg: fewer rotatable bonds (stiffer chains) give higher Tg.

title: Polymer Informatics Prediction of Tg from Chemical Structure (QSPR-GAP)
abstract: A combined group-additivity and QSPR framework predicts Tg of poly(aryl ether ketone)s (median RMSE 8 K); submonomer aromatic motifs contribute additively to Tg, with rigid aryl/ketone units raising it.

title: Triptycene-based polyimides with tunable high fractional free volume
abstract: Rigid, bulky triptycene units inserted into polyimide backbones raise fractional free volume by frustrating chain packing, giving high gas permeability; substituent size tunes FFV and the free-volume size distribution.

title: Molecular design of free volume in thermally rearranged polybenzoxazole membranes
abstract: Increasing steric hindrance of bridging groups in the dianhydride monomer enlarges pore radius and number, raising fractional free volume (FFV); gas permeability correlates positively with FFV.

title: Polyphenylsulfone copolymer membranes: structure effects on free volume and permeation
abstract: Bulky tetramethyl-biphenol units increase inter-chain spacing and fractional free volume (FFV); methyl groups both raise free volume and rigidify chains, increasing permeability while holding selectivity.

title: Free volume and permeability correlations in high-free-volume glassy polymers
abstract: Fractional free volume (FFV), the unoccupied space between chains (Bondi theory), is estimated from cryogenic sorption and the NELF model; FFV relates to characteristic density and correlates well with gas permeability across polymer families.

title: Halogen substitution to fine-tune fractional free volume of microporous polyimides
abstract: Introducing F, Cl, Br at the ortho position tunes interchain cavity and fractional free volume of PIM-polyimides; larger van der Waals volume of the halogen raises FFV and gas permeability.

title: Intrinsic Thermal Conductivity of Molecular Engineered Polymers
abstract: Intrinsic thermal conductivity of isotropic polymers is typically ~0.2 W/mK; enhancing inter-chain supramolecular interactions and forming crystalline or liquid-crystalline order are the main strategies to raise it.

title: Role of Chain Morphology and Stiffness in Thermal Conductivity of Amorphous Polymers
abstract: In amorphous polymers thermal conductivity is a strong function of the chain radius of gyration and persistence length: stiffer chains with larger persistence length adopt extended conformations and conduct heat better; rigid rod-like chains can crystallize and raise conductivity by an order of magnitude.

title: Thermal Conductivity of Conjugated Polymers for Thermoelectrics
abstract: Across 17 conjugated materials, thermal conductivity increases with stiffer backbones, higher molecular weight and heavier repeat units in ordered polymers; in amorphous polymers it correlates negatively with persistence length and repeat-unit mass.

title: Machine-learning discovery of polymer structures with high thermal conductivity
abstract: Machine-learning models trained on molecular-dynamics thermal conductivity of single-chain polymers, using fingerprint representations of repeat units, reveal structure-conductivity relationships and identify hypothetical high-conductivity polymers.

title: Thermal conductivity of polymers and polymer nanocomposites (review)
abstract: Reviews molecular-level thermal transport in polymers in terms of morphology, chain structure and inter-chain coupling; the intrinsically low thermal conductivity of polymers is a barrier for electronics packaging and heat exchangers.

title: Mean-square radius of gyration of polymer chains
abstract: A unified expression for the mean-square radius of gyration of polymer chains with side groups/heteroatoms; for degree of polymerization above ~100 the dependence follows <S2> = a M^b, consistent with experiment.

title: Conformations of Ring Polystyrenes in Bulk Studied by SANS
abstract: Small-angle neutron scattering on ring polystyrenes (10-400 kg/mol) gives radius of gyration scaling Rg ~ N^0.47, smaller than the Gaussian-chain exponent 0.5, reflecting compact ring conformations.

title: Effect of molecular weight on conformational characteristics of poly(3-hexylthiophene)
abstract: Light-scattering and RIS modeling of P3HT give radius of gyration vs molecular weight; persistence length approaches ~3 nm at high MW, and bulky hexyl side chains expand the chains relative to unsubstituted polythiophene.

title: Molecular dimensions of polystyrene in the bulk by neutron diffraction
abstract: Low-angle neutron scattering gives a radius of gyration of ~90 A for bulk polystyrene at M=97,200, in agreement with unperturbed (theta) chain dimensions.

title: Molecular weight dependence of radius of gyration of partially hydrolyzed polyacrylamide
abstract: For ultra-high-MW HPAM in good solvent, static/dynamic light scattering give the coil-size scaling Rg = 3.52e-2 Mw^0.51, linking molecular weight to radius of gyration.
